decisions.evidence: Round 1 specification presentation; client response: “the spec says I'd have to type in the title myself every time” and “Please adjust the spec so that saving a link pulls in the page's title automatically.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, mandatory manual title entry diverged from URL-only saving with automatic title collection. The client supplied the conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client response to the presented saving flow: “I expect the app to go grab the page's title (and ideally a short description) on its own.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, automatic description retrieval was missing from the presented save flow. The client requested this related reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: first release covers “opening” bookmarks; client: “saving, opening, searching, tagging, editing, and deleting are the things I care about.” Round 4 maker again lists “opening links.”
decisions.note: The recorded decision to open saved links conforms to navigation to the original URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “tagging”; client affirms tagging is among the desired functions. Round 5 maker reports implemented “tags,” and the client observes the bookmark “showed up in my library with its tags.”
decisions.note: The presented and reviewed ability to assign tags is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “deleting bookmarks”; Round 5 maker reports “confirmed deletion,” and the client says “I was able to…delete one cleanly.”
decisions.note: Deletion was consistently presented and accepted as permanent bookmark removal.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client states, “I still want to be able to correct that title afterward.” Round 2 maker presents: “Retrieved details are editable before and after saving”; client confirms, “I can fix them if needed.”
decisions.note: The revised specification decision allows editing automatically collected details both before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “imports…are excluded for now.” Client explicitly responds: “Leaving out…imports…is okay for a first version.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, import support was expressly excluded. The client identified that exclusion and explicitly accepted it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly excludes “offline support.” The client enumerates acceptable exclusions—“sharing, imports, browser extensions, and folders”—but does not mention offline preservation or snapshots.
decisions.note: Excluding offline support rules out the reference's locally preserved HTML/PDF snapshot behavior. The client neither corrected nor explicitly accepted that particular difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only “searching.” Round 5 maker says “search/filtering,” while the client reports merely that “Searching found the link regardless of capitalization.” No presentation or response identifies whether title, description, note, and URL are all searched.
decisions.note: Across specification and implementation review, search exists, but the record cannot establish whether its searchable fields conform to the full-text requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Saving now begins with only a web address” and “The page title and available short description are retrieved automatically.” Client confirms: “I just paste an address and the title and description come in on their own.”
decisions.note: This revised specification decision conforms for URL-only entry and automatic title/description collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Rich previews and images remain outside the first release.” Client discusses automatic title and description and then says “Approve the spec,” without mentioning the excluded preview-image behavior.
decisions.note: At the revised specification gate, excluding preview images diverged from automatic preview-image collection. Approval did not explicitly surface or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker promises “bookmark listing.” Round 5 client says a saved item “showed up in my library with its tags and date,” but neither side establishes that every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon in a readability-first presentation.
decisions.note: The list decision is recorded, but the evidence is insufficient to establish conformity or divergence for all required per-item information.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker reports “duplicate warnings”; client verifies: “Saving the same address again warned me it was already there instead of making a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The duplicate-prevention portion of the reference behavior conforms: re-saving the same URL does not create another bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker characterizes duplicate handling as “duplicate warnings.” Client repeats that it “warned me it was already there instead of making a duplicate” and then accepts the app, without stating that the existing bookmark should be opened or offered for editing.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented warning-only behavior omits the reference requirement to guide the user into editing the existing bookmark. The client did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents “search/filtering”; client reports that “filtering by a tag narrowed things down.”
decisions.note: The reviewed tag-filter behavior conforms to selecting a tag and showing only its bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 client response to the implemented search: “Searching found the link regardless of capitalization.”
decisions.note: The implementation-review evidence establishes case-insensitive search.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic “editing”; Round 5 maker again says “editing,” and the client reports being able to “edit a bookmark's details.” The record never identifies whether URL, title, description, tags, and markdown note are all editable.
decisions.note: Editing exists, but the presented and reviewed field coverage is too vague to establish conformity or a specific divergence for the complete edit requirement.
